## Source 1 — arXiv 2508.04721: "Toward Low-Latency End-to-End Voice Agents for Telecommunications" (NetoAI 4-model cascade)

**Type:** Academic preprint (arXiv, Aug 2025)
**Headline:** "Toward Low-Latency End-to-End Voice Agents for Telecommunications Using Streaming ASR, Quantized LLMs, and Real-Time TTS"

### Verbatim excerpts:
> "We introduce a low-latency telecom AI voice agent pipeline for real-time, interactive telecommunications use, enabling advanced voice AI for call center automation, intelligent IVR (Interactive Voice Response), and AI-driven customer support."
> "The solution is built for telecom, combining four specialized models by NetoAI: TSLAM, a 4-bit quantized Telecom-Specific Large Language Model (LLM); T-VEC, a Telecom-Specific Embedding Model; TTE, a Telecom-Specific Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) model; and T-Synth, a Te..."

### Pain points (verbatim audience language):
- End-to-end voice agents lack deep reasoning; cascaded pipelines have high latency
- 4-bit quantization is the frontier for fitting telecom-grade LLMs into sub-second latency
- The 4-model cascade (TSLAM + T-VEC + TTE + T-Synth) is the new architecture pattern

### Why this works:
The arXiv paper is the academic backbone for the persona's "sub-700ms is the ceiling" anchor. The 4-bit quantized TSLAM is the technical differentiator — most LLM-backed voice agents use full-precision GPT-4-class models that hit 900ms+. The Pillar 4 angle: "The voice agents hitting sub-500ms in 2026 are running 4-bit quantized telecom-specific LLMs, not GPT-4. Here's the architecture difference." **Cross-link to the persona's Example 9 voice anchor: the 480ms number was hit by switching to gpt-4o-mini (a similar quantization trade-off).**

## Source 2 — arXiv 2601.19952: "LTS-VoiceAgent: A Listen-Think-Speak Framework for Efficient Streaming Voice Interaction via Semantic Triggering and Incremental Reasoning" (Jan 2026)

**Type:** Academic preprint (arXiv, Jan 2026)
**Headline:** "LTS-VoiceAgent: A Listen-Think-Speak Framework for Efficient Streaming Voice Interaction via Semantic Triggering and Incremental Reasoning"

### Verbatim excerpts:
> "Real-time voice agents face a dilemma: end-to-end models often lack deep reasoning, while cascaded pipelines incur high latency by executing ASR, LLM reasoning, and TTS strictly in sequence, unlike human conversation where listeners often start thinking before the speaker finishes."
> "Since cascaded architectures remain the dominant choice for complex tasks, existing cascaded streaming strategies attempt to reduce this latency via mechanical segmentation (e.g., fixed ch..."

### Pain points (verbatim audience language):
- The LLM-reasoning latency is the dominant bottleneck in cascaded pipelines
- "Mechanical segmentation" (fixed chunk boundaries) doesn't work — human conversation doesn't have fixed chunk boundaries
- Semantic triggering (start thinking when the speaker pauses semantically, not temporally) is the new frontier

### Why this works:
The Listen-Think-Speak framing maps directly to the persona's "Listen. Think. Speak." semantic-triggering insight. The arXiv paper formalizes what the persona's voice anchor describes intuitively. The Pillar 4 angle: "The cascaded pipeline is the dominant architecture. The LLM-reasoning step is the bottleneck. The fix isn't faster models — it's semantic triggering. Start thinking when the caller pauses semantically, not when the VAD timer hits 600ms." **Strongest Pillar 4 cross-link with the persona's Example 9 voice anchor — the LTS framework is the academic version of the build-log insight.**
